claims.text: Untreated W–Cu composites are prone to phase separation during sintering and subsequent high-temperature or irradiation service.
Untreated W–Cu composites are prone to interfacial void formation during sintering and subsequent service.
Phase separation and interfacial voids reduce the thermal conductivity of W–Cu composites.
A roughly 100–200 nm electroless Ni coating should be deposited on W surfaces before composite consolidation.
The Ni-coated composite should be sintered at 800–1000 °C under a controlled reducing atmosphere.
The Ni coating will form a graded diffusion-mediated interlayer at the W/Cu interface during sintering.
During sintering, Ni will partially diffuse into tungsten.
During sintering, Ni will partially diffuse into copper.
The transitional Ni interlayer will minimize the Kirkendall effect.
The transitional Ni interlayer will suppress interfacial void nucleation.
The Ni-modified interface will suppress phase separation.
A graded Ni-containing interface will better accommodate thermal-expansion mismatch between W and Cu.
Better accommodation of thermal-expansion mismatch will reduce interfacial decohesion under high heat flux and irradiation.
Ni-modified W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity than untreated W–Cu under the proposed service conditions.
Ni-modified W–Cu will have better interfacial mechanical integrity than untreated W–Cu.
Ni-modified W–Cu will exhibit fewer interfacial voids than untreated W–Cu after heat-transfer and irradiation exposure.
The proposed treatment is applicable when service temperatures do not exceed approximately 600–700 °C under irradiation.
Precise control of Ni thickness and diffusion is required to avoid detrimental brittle intermetallic phases.
The scalability and coating uniformity of electroless Ni plating across complex W–Cu geometries remain unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The intervention labels the 100–200 nm coating as optimized, while the uncertainty field states that the optimal coating thickness and sintering profile are not yet known.
